practices.practice: Read the DocumentDB connection string from an environment variable or secret provider at runtime and never commit credentials or connection strings to source control.
practices.prior_belief: Read the DocumentDB/Mongo connection string only from an environment variable (DOCUMENTDB_URI) or a secrets provider at runtime; never commit credentials, connection strings, or API keys to source control or plaintext files.
practices.source_name: Quickstart: Connect Mongoose to Azure DocumentDB
practices.how_found: Azure DocumentDB connection string environment variable best practices DOCUMENTDB_URI

practices.practice: Create one long-lived MongoClient per process (a singleton) and reuse it across requests rather than creating a client per request.
practices.prior_belief: Use a single, long-lived MongoClient (connection pool) instance per process (create it at app startup and reuse it for all requests) instead of creating a new client per request; close it cleanly on shutdown.

practices.practice: Always use TLS for connections and restrict access with network controls (Private Endpoint / VNet or firewall rules) rather than relying only on username/password.
practices.prior_belief: Enable TLS/SSL for connections and validate server certificates (use secure=true / tls=true options), and restrict access with network controls (VNet/private endpoint or IP firewall) rather than relying solely on username/password.

practices.practice: Store each branch's rolled-up summary as one document targeted by branchId and maintain it with targeted updateOne(..., upsert:true); use a unique index on the branch id when branchId is the natural key.
practices.prior_belief: Store cached branch summaries as one document per branch with a unique index on branch_id so you can maintain/refresh a branch summary using updateOne(..., upsert=True) targeted by branch_id.

practices.practice: If you want automatic expiry of rolled-up caches, create a TTL index on a Date field (e.g., lastRefreshed) with expireAfterSeconds; TTL requires the field be a Date and cannot be a compound or multikey index.
practices.prior_belief: Create a TTL index on the branch_summaries collection (or on a last_refreshed field) when you want automatic expiry of rolled-up caches, and set retention by expireAfterSeconds so stale summaries are removed automatically.

practices.practice: Create compound indexes that match the aggregation pipeline's $match shape (apply the ESR rule: Equality → Sort → Range) so aggregation can use indexes before expensive stages like $facet.
practices.prior_belief: For the transactions collection, create compound indexes that match the $match stage of the aggregation pipelines (e.g., { branch_id: 1, transaction_date: 1 } and any other frequently filtered fields) so aggregation can use indexes before $facet.

practices.practice: Push restrictive $match and $project stages as early as possible in aggregation pipelines and include only fields needed by subsequent stages to reduce memory and CPU during $facet and grouping.
practices.prior_belief: Push restrictive $match and $project stages as early as possible in aggregation pipelines and include only the fields needed by subsequent stages to reduce memory and CPU during $facet and grouping.

practices.practice: When running heavy aggregation pipelines, set allowDiskUse=true (or the driver equivalent) and test with explain() so operations that need disk spill are allowed and to avoid memory rejection; use paged or incremental refresh for very large datasets.
practices.prior_belief: When running heavy aggregation pipelines, set allowDiskUse=True (or the driver equivalent) and test with explain() to ensure operations won't be rejected for memory; use paged or incremental refresh for very large datasets.

practices.practice: Use explain("executionStats") and the MCP or diagnostic tools to inspect query and aggregation plans (IXSCAN vs COLLSCAN, keysExamined/docsExamined) and fix COLLSCANs before shipping.
practices.prior_belief: Use explain() and the cluster's MCP/monitoring tools to inspect query and aggregation plans and verify which indexes are used; record and act on any COLLSCAN warnings before shipping.

practices.practice: Implement retries with exponential backoff for transient network errors and rate-limiting responses, and prefer idempotent operations when retrying to avoid duplicates.
practices.prior_belief: Implement retries with exponential backoff for transient network errors and rate-limiting responses; prefer idempotent operations (upsert) or include a retry token for non-idempotent operations to avoid duplicates.

practices.practice: Enable driver retryableReads/retryableWrites when supported and set sensible timeouts (connectTimeoutMS, serverSelectionTimeoutMS) so the app fails fast under misconfiguration instead of hanging.
practices.prior_belief: Enable retryableWrites and retryReads on the Mongo client when supported, and set reasonable serverSelectionTimeoutMS/connectTimeoutMS so the app fails fast during misconfiguration instead of hanging.

practices.practice: For a refresh job, perform an atomic per-branch upsert (updateOne with filter on branchId and upsert:true) so refreshes are safe if retried or interrupted.
practices.prior_belief: For the cached summaries refresh job, perform an atomic upsert per branch (updateOne with filter on branch_id and upsert:true) so refreshes are safe if retried or interrupted; avoid multi-document partial updates unless wrapped in a transaction.
practices.source_name: Quickstart: Use Azure DocumentDB with MongoDB driver for Python

practices.practice: Avoid multi-document transactions unless necessary: prefer single-document designs or eventual-consistency update patterns and use multi-document transactions only after evaluating latency/throughput impact.
practices.prior_belief: If you need to update multiple documents atomically (e.g., update summary and a related metadata doc), use multi-document transactions only when necessary and test latency/throughput impact; prefer single-document design to avoid transactions when possible.

practices.practice: Create indexes on fields used for top-N queries or dashboard sorts (or create a compound index matching equality+sort) to avoid in-memory sorts and speed ordered list endpoints.
practices.prior_belief: Create an index on fields used for top-N queries or sorts in the dashboard (e.g., { branch_id: 1, avg_ticket: -1 }) to avoid in-memory sorts and speed up list endpoints that order by metrics in branch_summaries.

practices.practice: When using vector search, store embeddings as numeric arrays and create a DocumentDB vector index with the exact dimensions and similarity (COS/L2/IP); prefer DiskANN for production scale and tune maxDegree, lBuild and query-time lSearch for the recall/latency tradeoff.
practices.prior_belief: If using vector search over embeddings, store embeddings as numeric arrays and create the cluster-provided vector index (DiskANN/HNSW/IVF) with matching dimension, metric (cosine/L2), and maxDimensions; test retrieval latency and recall on representative data.

practices.practice: Keep third-party API keys (OpenAI, embedding providers) out of the repository and require them as runtime secrets (e.g., OPENAI_API_KEY) so the app has a clear no-op fallback in tests/CI.
practices.prior_belief: Keep OpenAI (or other LLM) API keys out of the repository and environment files committed to source control; require OPENAI_API_KEY at runtime or provide a clear no-op fallback in tests and CI so the app doesn't accidentally call external APIs during verification.

practices.practice: Rate-limit and validate user inputs on expensive endpoints (e.g., refresh and ask); authenticate and authorize refresh operations to avoid accidental large refresh jobs or expensive LLM/vector queries from untrusted callers.
practices.prior_belief: Rate-limit and validate user inputs to the /refresh and /ask endpoints (authenticate/authorize refresh operations) to avoid accidental large refresh jobs or prompting expensive vector/LLM queries from untrusted callers.
practices.how_found: Azure DocumentDB rate limit API protect endpoints; DocumentDB rate limiting recommendations; DocumentDB DoS protection application rate limiting

practices.practice: Monitor collection- and cluster-level metrics (CPU, memory, IOPS, storage, connections), enable slow-query logging/diagnostics to Log Analytics, and add alerts for sustained saturation or throttling so you can scale or optimize indexes proactively.
practices.prior_belief: Monitor collection-level metrics, RU/compute usage, latency and throttling in the cloud console (or MCP tools), and add alerts for sustained high CPU/IO or throttling so you can scale the cluster or optimize indexes before dashboards degrade.

practices.practice: Prefer the DocumentDB search index + $search (createSearchIndexes + $search) and BM25 scoring for full-text search; use fuzzy/phrase settings and custom analyzers rather than the community $text operator.

Enable in-region HA (availability-zone placement) for production clusters to get the 99.99% SLA and add a cross-region replica for 99.995% SLA when you need DR; understand the synchronous in-region model vs asynchronous cross-region replica RPO.
Keep an index budget per collection (review $indexStats) and prefer 5–15 well-chosen indexes; hide/drop unused indexes rather than accumulating overlapping single-field indexes.

notes: I inspected the app to learn which areas matter (connection/auth, aggregation/upsert, indexes, caching, simple lexical retrieval and optional vector/LLM integration) and then searched public Microsoft docs and the installed DocumentDB skills. Almost all prior beliefs (K01–K16, K18, etc.) are confirmed by Azure DocumentDB public docs or the installed skill guidance; only K17 (rate-limiting/endpoint hardening) is an application-level prior belief for which I found no Azure-DocumentDB-specific public guidance and so it is listed as prior_knowledge_only. Installed skills were used as authoritative sources for index, vector, connection, security, and monitoring guidance; Microsoft Learn pages provide confirmation for aggregation options (allowDiskUse), upsert semantics, and quickstart secret-handling guidance.
